# Citation

Gaynor, R. C., et al. (2021). *AlphaSimR: an R package for breeding program simulations*. G3: Genes, Genomes, Genetics. DOI: 10.1093/g3journal/jkab130. Source: [https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8022926/](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8022926/).

# One-Sentence Summary

Describes AlphaSimR, an R framework for stochastic breeding-program simulation that models genomes, crosses, traits, selection, and breeding operations.

# Scope for simitall

Use as a complementary breeding-engine option, especially for multi-cycle selection experiments. simitall should expose a stable higher-level workflow rather than duplicate every engine feature.

# Agent-Safe Takeaways

- Breeding simulation separates founder generation, meiosis, crossing, phenotyping, selection, and advancement.
- Quantitative traits can include multiple genetic-effect classes and environmental variation.
- Simulation is most useful when output QC is compared with intended breeding-population properties.

# Inputs to Specify

- Founder haplotypes or simulated founder genomes
- Genetic maps and chromosome structure
- Trait architecture and breeding-cycle design

# Expected Outputs

- Line genotypes and pedigrees
- Phenotypes and breeding values
- Selection and genetic-gain summaries

# Limitations and Guardrails

- Engine defaults are not a substitute for species-specific recombination and trait assumptions.
- Validate simulated LD, heterozygosity, family structure, and response to selection.

# Questions This Record Can Ground

- When should a workflow use AlphaSimR versus the simuPOP bridge?
- Which outputs are needed to evaluate genetic gain and diversity across cycles?
